title: Local runtime config transpiler — brain dump and sketch
body:
Purpose and motivation:

This is a personal sketch for a lightweight "transpiler" that takes a single, user-facing runtime configuration (the "developer config") and emits environment-specific runtime configs for local dev, edge-proxy, dedicated pools, and private deployments. The goal is to make the local development experience faithful enough to production routing, batching, and fallback semantics without forcing engineers to maintain multiple hand-rolled YAMLs per environment.

Why we need this (pain points):
- engineers keep duplicated config files for local/dev/staging/prod; drift causes surprising behavior during rollouts
- local runners often skip critical fallbacks (e.g., model-variant routing, cache warmers) which hides regressions
- ops has special annotations (node selectors, taints, KMS keys) that shouldn't be exposed to devs but are required for private deploy manifests
- we want an explainable transform so infra and product can reason about what was changed when generating a target manifest

Non-goals:
- this is not a policy engine or secrets manager (it will reference secrets by id, not store them)
- not trying to replace full infrastructure templating (helm/terraform), but to produce lightweight runtime overlays consumed by our local runner and edge proxies

High-level design:
1) Single canonical developer-config (YAML/JSON). Human-editable, focused on application intent: model preference list, latency SLO, cache hints, soft fallback policy, route hints, instrumentation sampling.
2) A set of environment profiles (local, dev-cluster, dedicated, private-vpc, hosted) with policy bundles. Profiles encode what extra keys or transformations to apply for a given environment.
3) A deterministic, ordered transform pipeline (passes): validation -> expand macros -> policy merge -> platform adapt -> optimization heuristics -> emit. Each pass produces a diff-like patch (for explainability).
4) Output artifacts: target config (JSON) and transform log (list of patches and rationale).

Core concepts and schema sketch (developer-config):
- name: string
- model_preferences: [ { name: string, variants: [string], preference: int } ]
- latency_slo_ms: int
- fallback_policy: { allow_model_substitution: bool, max_quality_drop_pct: int, prefer_quantized: bool }
- cache: { enabled: bool, prefix_whitelist: [string], kv_ttl_s: int }
- batching: { mode: auto|manual|off, max_tokens: int, max_batch_ms: int }
- routing_hints: [ { selector: string, prefer_region: string, prefer_tier: string } ]
- telemetry: { sampling_rate: float, include_prompt_snippet: bool }
- dev_overrides: { prefer_local_mock: bool, local_kv_size_mb: int }

Example developer-config (YAML as free text):

---
name: notes-app
model_preferences:
  - name: base-chat
    variants: [redwood-chat-1b, redwood-chat-350m]
    preference: 0
latency_slo_ms: 150
fallback_policy:
  allow_model_substitution: true
  max_quality_drop_pct: 20
  prefer_quantized: true
cache:
  enabled: true
  prefix_whitelist: ["/api/notes", "/api/search"]
  kv_ttl_s: 3600
batching:
  mode: auto
  max_tokens: 1024
  max_batch_ms: 8
routing_hints:
  - selector: tenant == "free-tier"
    prefer_region: us-west1
    prefer_tier: dedicated
telemetry:
  sampling_rate: 0.01
  include_prompt_snippet: false
dev_overrides:
  prefer_local_mock: true
  local_kv_size_mb: 256
---

Transform rules (informal):
- Validation pass: ensure required keys present; warn if latency_slo < 20ms or > 2000ms.
- Macro expansion: $MODEL_REGISTRY -> map to canonical ids in profile.
- Policy merge: overlay environment profile defaults (e.g., private-vpc injects kms_key and logging sinks).
- Platform adapt: convert generic batching.max_tokens -> platform-specific batch-window tokens & concurrency settings (e.g., in local runner, max_batch_size = min(max_tokens/64, 8)).
- Optimization heuristics: if prefer_quantized and hardware != gpu, prefer CPU-optimized quant model variant; if latency_slo < 100ms, add warmup hint with top-1 prefix cache.

Example output (local profile) as JSON (shortened):
{
  "service_name": "notes-app.local",
  "model": { "name": "redwood-chat-350m-quant", "runtime_hint": "cpu-quant" },
  "batching": { "mode": "auto", "max_batch_items": 6, "max_wait_ms": 8 },
  "cache": { "enabled": true, "kv_size_mb": 256, "ttl_s": 3600 },
  "telemetry": { "sampling_rate": 0.01 },
  "fallback": { "enabled": true, "max_quality_drop_pct": 20 }
}

Explainability artifacts:
- Each transform pass emits an entry: {pass: name, reason: text, patch: unified-diff-like-string}.
- The runner can surface the transform log on startup (--show-config-diff) so devs see exactly what changed from their developer-config to runtime-config.

Heuristics and local runner specifics:
- prefer_local_mock: if true, produce a local-tooling stub entry pointing at :9001 and set model runtime to "mock". Useful for UI integration tests.
- local_kv_size_mb: overrides cache.kv_size_mb and sets eviction_policy=LRU for local runner.
- If caching is enabled and developer-config.cache.prefix_whitelist empty, default to safe prefixes (/api/search, /api/doc).
- If latency_slo_ms < 100, set ttl-prefetch-window to 10% of ttl or 10s min.

Edge cases and merging semantics:
- Explicit vs implicit: explicit fields in developer-config should always win over profile defaults. Profiles can only add if key absent or when explicit allow_profile_override is set.
- Lists: model_preferences merging is positional merge by preference value; profile additions append but cannot re-order explicit preference values.
- Secret IDs: If private profile, inject kms_key_id as profile.secret.kms_key_id but never materialize secret contents.

Pipeline ASCII diagram (linear view):

[developer-config.yaml] --> [validation] --> [macro expansion] --> [policy-merge(profile:local)] --> [platform-adapt(pass=local-runner)] --> [heuristics-optimize] --> [emit runtime.json + transform-log.txt]

Open questions / TODOs (brain dump):
- canonical schema versioning: how to manage backward compatibility as we add new developer-config fields? Need a small version tag in developer-config and transformations that declare supported range.
- conflict resolution UX: when profile attempts to override an explicit developer intent, surface a concise actionable warning with suggestion.
- integration with console: should transform logs be stored as artifact for rollout audits? For hosted maybe yes, for private maybe optional.
- policy composition: will we support multiple profiles composed (e.g., local + privacy-sandbox)? If yes, need deterministic ordering and conflict resolution rules.
- performance: transpiler should be fast (<50ms) for local runner hot reload. Keep transforms simple and cache compiled transforms keyed by hash of developer-config + profile.

Quick prototyping checklist (next steps):
- implement prototype CLI (node/ts) that accepts dev-config.json + profile and emits runtime.json + transform-log.txt
- write a small set of profile files for: local, cloud-dev, dedicated, private-vpc
- run integration tests with local-runner to ensure fallback_policy semantics preserved
- add a "--explain" flag to local-runner to surface transform diffs in human format

Notes to self (short reminders):
- keep transform passes idempotent (applying same profile twice shouldn't change outcome)
- prefer readable diffs: show original block + new block, not just automated patch hunks
- make sure telemetry sampling conversions are stable (0.01 -> 1%) across profiles

Example transform log fragment (human friendly):
- [validation] ok: latency_slo_ms=150 in acceptable range
- [macro expansion] $MODEL_REGISTRY.redwood-chat-350m -> redwood-chat-350m-20250401 (pinned snapshot)
- [policy-merge:local] set service_name suffix ".local"; set local_kv_size_mb=256 (from dev_overrides)
- [platform-adapt:local-runner] compute max_batch_items=6 from max_tokens 1024 (rule: tokens/128, cap 8)

Thoughts on API shape for eventual service:
- POST /transpile?profile=local body: developer-config (json) -> 200 {runtime_config: {...}, transform_log: [...]}
- support dry-run header: X-Dry-Run: true -> returns only transform_log and warnings
- auth: only internal tokens permit profiles that inject secrets (private)

Small example of a platform-adapt rule expressed as pseudocode:
if profile == 'local' and batching.mode == 'auto':
  max_batch_items = min(ceil(batching.max_tokens / 128), 8)
  max_wait_ms = batching.max_batch_ms || 8

End of sketch. This is intentionally informal — want to iterate with Ethan/Liang and SRE to lock down merge semantics and a small spec for the transform log format.

Unresolved: do we want to canonicalize on JSON or keep YAML for readability? Probably accept YAML and internally parse to canonical JSON for diffs.

If I forget next week: run a quick prototype + test with notes-app dev-config and demonstrate local runner shows same fallback path as dedicated pool.
summary: Personal draft for a local runtime config transpiler that converts a single developer-config into environment-specific runtime config + explainability logs. Includes schema sketch, transform pipeline, heuristics, examples, open questions, and next steps.
